title: Least-squares regression & residuals
examples: How do I know if the relationship is actually straight?
What does the value of r tell me about the data?
Can I use residuals to check my model?

explain.say: Today we look at the line of best fit. This line helps us predict one thing from another.

draw.text: Line of Best Fit: y = a + bx

explain.say: The equation for this line is y equals a plus b x. Here, b is the slope, and a is the y-intercept.
Next we look at r and r squared. The correlation coefficient, r, measures the strength and direction of the linear relationship.
R squared tells us the proportion of the variance in y explained by x. It is always a number between zero and one.
Finally, we examine residual plots. A residual is the difference between the actual value and the predicted value.

faq.q: What does a low r value mean for my data?
faq.a: A low r value suggests a weak linear relationship between the variables. This means the data points are scattered far from a straight line.
asks: What if r is close to zero?
Does a small r mean no relationship?

faq.q: If r squared is 0 point 81, what does that mean?
faq.a: It means that eighty one percent of the variation in the y variable is accounted for by the x variable through the model. This is a strong fit.
asks: How do I interpret r squared?

faq.q: How do I know if a straight line is appropriate?
faq.a: You check the residual plot. If the points look randomly scattered around zero, the linear model is probably appropriate. If they curve, it is not.
asks: What should the residual plot look like?
Should the residuals form a pattern?

faq.q: What is the difference between r and r squared?
faq.a: R is the correlation coefficient, which measures direction and strength. R squared is the coefficient of determination, which is a proportion of variance.
asks: Are r and r squared the same thing?
Which one do I use for percentage?

faq.q: Can I use this method if the relationship is curved?
faq.a: No, least-squares regression assumes a linear relationship. If the data curves, you should consider a different mathematical model.
asks: What if the graph is curved?

facts: The line of best fit uses least squares to minimize the sum of squared residuals.
The correlation coefficient r ranges from negative one to positive one.
R squared is calculated by squaring the value of r.
A residual plot should show residuals scattered randomly around the horizontal axis at zero.

quiz.say: If the residual plot shows a clear U shape, the linear model is:

options.show: Only appropriate if r is high
options.say: Only appropriate if r is high

quiz.why: A curved pattern indicates a non-linear relationship, so the straight line model is not the best fit.

wrong.0: This is tempting because the points are still somewhat centered around the line.
wrong.1: R only measures strength, not the shape of the underlying relationship.
wrong.2: The shape of the residuals is more important than just the correlation value.

quiz.say: If r squared is 0 point 64, what does this suggest about the data?

options.show: Sixty-four percent of the variation in y is explained by x.
options.say: Sixty-four percent of the variation in y is explained by x.

quiz.why: R squared directly gives the proportion of variance explained, which is sixty-four percent in this case.

wrong.0: R is the square root of r squared, not the same value.
wrong.1: A value of zero point six four shows a moderate relationship, not a perfect one.
wrong.3: The slope is a separate calculation and is not the same as r squared.

quiz.say: A residual value of negative five means:

options.show: The x value was too high
options.say: The x value was too high

options.show: The actual value was five units below the predicted value.
options.say: The actual value was five units below the predicted value.

quiz.why: A negative residual means the actual data point fell below the line of best fit.

wrong.0: The steepness relates to the slope, not the residual at one point.
wrong.1: One negative residual does not mean the entire model is incorrect.
wrong.2: The residual compares the y-value, not the x-value, to the line.
